extends: the v1-v4 research files, which are not modified
grade_policy: No feeding grade is assigned in the research layer. A record here is not a statement that the plant is safe to feed.

sources.citation: Ritz, J., Griebeler, E.M., Huber, R., Clauss, M. 2010. Body size development of captive and free-ranging African spurred tortoises (Geochelone sulcata): high plasticity in reptilian growth rates. Herpetological Journal 20:213-216.
sources.method: growth records of three captive-bred animals weighed over almost 18 years at a private breeding facility; the diet is described in the methods, not measured
sources.what_was_read: whole article (open access PDF from the society)

sources.citation: Mahmoud, Z.N., El Naiem, D.A. 1988. Studies on the growth of the desert tortoise (Testudo sulcata) in Sudan: changes in morphometrics and body weight from hatching to one year (0+). Herpetological Journal 1:280-284.
sources.method: 16 hatchlings from one clutch kept in an enclosure for a year and measured; food offered every other day
sources.what_was_read: methods paragraph in the PDF text layer. The scanned page image is too faint to read, so the two plant names are given as the text layer prints them and were not checked against the image
